title: Joining Ontario's home renovation rebate program
subtitle: Heritage permit approved for a Victoria Park boathouse kitchen addition; closed session held on two confidential matters.
overview: Council voted to join the provincial Home Renovations Savings Program through a one-window approach run with Enbridge Gas and the Independent Electric System Operator {{vote:m1}}. Kitchener Utilities customers will be able to apply for rebates on upgrades such as windows, doors, insulation, air sealing, heat pumps and solar. Staff expect the program to start in the fall. Council also directed staff to build the rebate funding into future utility budgets, which staff said is a significant financial commitment.

Council approved a heritage permit for a rear addition at 57 Jubilee Drive, an outdoor kitchen serving the boathouse patio in Victoria Park {{vote:m2}}. The final building permit must be reviewed by the City's Heritage Planner first. Staff said they are still discussing a lower parapet height with the applicant.

Council then met in closed session to consider competitive position, contracts and negotiations, and a solicitor-client privilege matter {{vote:m3}}. The minutes report no further outcome from that session.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to join the provincial program through a one-window approach with Enbridge Gas and the Independent Electric System Operator, authorized a service agreement with Enbridge, and directed that rebate funding be included in future Kitchener Utilities budgets.
Council approved a heritage permit for a rear addition under the Ontario Heritage Act, on condition that the Heritage Planner reviews and approves the final building permit before it is issued.

debate: On the rebate program, staff said the City would fund rebates while Enbridge handles applications for the province. Rebates would be consistent across Ontario and worth up to $5,000 per customer. Staff said higher incentives tend to increase uptake.

The CAO said the recommended option has a significant budget impact. It fits the City's climate goals, and the province clearly wanted utilities to join. Council has generally aligned with provincial approaches where possible.

One councillor asked about covering upgrades made earlier in 2025 after residents called. Staff said rebates would not be retroactive because the budget did not include them and the program requires pre- and post-upgrade audits. Staff offered to look into how many people it might affect.

Councillors asked about reaching seniors and about condos and rentals. Staff said marketing could include utility bill inserts, and that any homeowner could apply for improvements to their property. Council also asked staff to raise federal support with the province.

On the heritage permit, one councillor raised concerns about the short-notice walk-on process at the advisory committee and about the addition's height compared with the boathouse roofline. Staff said the notice was waived by committee vote because of the business's patio season timing. They said the design mirrors the existing addition and the parapet height is still being discussed. Others supported it for its contribution to Victoria Park.
